title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر الشريط السادس تابع
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikar fi Mustalah Ahl al-Athar — Tape Six, continued
body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وصلى الله وسلم على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه أجمعين، أما بعد فيقول الحافظ رحمه الله: \"ثم الطعن إما أن يكون لكذب الراوي أو تهمته بذلك أو فحش غلطه أو غفلته أو فسقه أو وهمه أو مخالفته أو جهالته أو بدعته أو سوء حفظه\" فذكر هنا هذه الأقسام من أقسام الطعن على حسب ترتيبه هو، وهو يختلف عن الترتيب الذي عليه جمهور أهل المصطلح، وهو الترتيب الذي سقناه سابقا، فتكون الأقسام به أقل من هذا التقسيم، لأن هذا التقسيم بعضه يشترك في الاسم، فذكره مع كونه مشتركا في الاسم كأقسام مما يزيد العدد من غير كبير فائدة، فلذلك لم ننتهج هذا لكن لا بأس بشرحه،
body_en:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and may God bless our Prophet Muhammad and grant him peace, and his family and his Companions all together. To proceed:

The Hafiz (may God have mercy on him) says: "Then the impugning of a narrator (ṭaʿn) is either on account of the narrator's lying, or his being suspected of that, or the grossness of his error, or his heedlessness, or his moral transgression (fisq), or his delusion (wahm), or his contradicting [more reliable narrators] (mukhālafah), or his being unknown (jahālah), or his innovation in religion (bidʿah), or his poor memory."

So he has mentioned here these categories among the categories of impugning, according to his own arrangement; and it differs from the arrangement followed by the majority of the specialists in hadith terminology, which is the arrangement we set out earlier. On that arrangement the categories come out fewer than on this division, because in this division some of the items share a single name; so for him to mention them, while they share a name, as separate categories is something that increases the number without much benefit. For that reason we did not adopt this arrangement — but there is no harm in expounding it,

The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this tape; the Arabic breaks off and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.
The text in quotation marks is the base text of Nukhbat al-Fikar being commented on; the unquoted text is the Sheikh's own commentary. The distinction is load-bearing and has been preserved.

The Sheikh is reporting the author's arrangement of the causes for impugning a narrator and contrasting it with the arrangement of the majority, stating his own preference for the latter. The excerpt ends before he expounds the individual categories.
